architectures.title: Request–response inference
architectures.description: A bounded prediction or generation behind an application interface.
architectures.fit: A single model call solves a well-scoped task.
architectures.tradeoff: Simple operation, but slow inference can exceed interface deadlines.
architectures.failure: Timeouts or malformed output: set deadlines, check schemas, and provide a deterministic fallback.
architectures.evaluation: Track end-to-end p95 latency, invalid outputs, and task success.
architectures.example: A web app classifies a support ticket.

architectures.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
architectures.description: Ground a generated answer in a maintained collection of evidence.
architectures.fit: Answers need information beyond model parameters.
architectures.tradeoff: Retrieval adds freshness and evidence, but also indexing and permission complexity.
architectures.failure: Missing evidence or unsupported claims: test retrieval separately and allow abstention.
architectures.evaluation: Measure evidence recall, citation support, and answer correctness on held-out questions.
architectures.example: A handbook assistant retrieves approved policy passages.

architectures.title: Tool-using agent loop
architectures.description: Let a model choose a bounded action, observe its result, and decide what follows.
architectures.fit: The next step depends on what the system discovers.
architectures.tradeoff: Flexible execution brings variable completion time and cost.
architectures.failure: Loops or unintended side effects: limit steps and require approval for consequential actions.
architectures.evaluation: Measure completion, tool errors, unsafe action attempts, and cost per task.
architectures.example: A desktop assistant investigates a problem through approved diagnostic tools.

architectures.title: Chained voice pipeline
architectures.description: Separate speech recognition, text reasoning, and spoken output.
architectures.fit: Inspectable text and control over each speech stage matter.
architectures.tradeoff: Stage-by-stage control adds latency and can propagate transcription mistakes.
architectures.failure: Misheard names or poor turn boundaries: confirm critical details and cancel interrupted playback.
architectures.evaluation: Measure transcription quality, first-audio latency, and interruption recovery.
architectures.example: A telephone assistant confirms a requested appointment date.

architectures.title: Realtime speech-to-speech
architectures.description: Stream audio to a model and spoken responses back through a continuous session.
architectures.fit: Natural conversational timing is central.
architectures.tradeoff: Connection state, buffering, and interruption management become core responsibilities.
architectures.failure: Talking over a person or playing stale output: cancel the current turn and reconcile session state.
architectures.evaluation: Measure response onset, turn completion, and barge-in success in noise.
architectures.example: A mobile language tutor supports quick spoken exchanges.

architectures.title: Wake-word gated assistant
architectures.description: A local trigger opens an intentional interaction with a speaker or wearable.
architectures.fit: A device waits for a short activation phrase.
architectures.tradeoff: Low-power listening balances missed activations against false triggers.
architectures.failure: Unwanted activation: provide a clear activity indicator, physical mute, and bounded retention.
architectures.evaluation: Test false accepts per listening hour, missed wakes, and power consumption.
architectures.example: A smart speaker activates a voice session after detecting a local trigger.

architectures.title: On-device inference
architectures.description: Run the model near the data without a required cloud round trip.
architectures.fit: Offline behavior or local data handling is essential.
architectures.tradeoff: Memory, battery, model size, and hardware support constrain quality.
architectures.failure: Thermal throttling or unsupported operations: test real hardware and provide compatible fallbacks.
architectures.evaluation: Measure energy per inference, memory, cold and warm latency, and task accuracy.
architectures.example: A phone recognizes objects without network connectivity.

architectures.title: Hybrid edge–cloud
architectures.description: Keep a local fast path and escalate selected work to remote inference.
architectures.fit: Local speed matters but some tasks exceed device capabilities.
architectures.tradeoff: Two paths complicate consistency and outage recovery.
architectures.failure: Unintended data transfer or unstable routing: define transfer permissions and explicit escalation rules.
architectures.evaluation: Compare local coverage, escalation rate, quality, and network-failure recovery.
architectures.example: A phone handles simple commands locally and escalates complex questions with permission.

architectures.title: Contextual application copilot
architectures.description: Bring selected application state into an assistant beside the work.
architectures.fit: Assistance should understand the current document or workflow.
architectures.tradeoff: Context improves relevance but can expose unrelated information.
architectures.failure: Stale or overbroad context: minimize selection, check permissions, and show a reviewable diff.
architectures.evaluation: Measure accepted suggestions, correction burden, and context-access errors.
architectures.example: An editor suggests a rewrite of selected text.

architectures.title: Browser & desktop action agent
architectures.description: Translate a goal into observed interface actions with repeated verification.
architectures.fit: A necessary system has a usable interface but no suitable API.
architectures.tradeoff: Layout changes and hidden state make interface automation brittle.
architectures.failure: Acting on the wrong control: verify preconditions and the resulting screen before continuing.
architectures.evaluation: Measure success across layout variations, recovery rate, and unauthorized actions.
architectures.example: An assistant navigates a legacy application with review before submission.

architectures.title: Event-driven AI worker
architectures.description: An event starts an independent, recoverable unit of AI work.
architectures.fit: Work should begin when a record or signal changes.
architectures.tradeoff: Queues decouple producers and workers but introduce eventual consistency.
architectures.failure: Duplicate processing or poison messages: use idempotency, bounded retries, and a dead-letter queue.
architectures.evaluation: Measure queue age, duplicate effects, completions, and exhausted retries.
architectures.example: A newly published document triggers automatic categorization.

architectures.title: Batch inference pipeline
architectures.description: Process a dataset on a schedule and publish versioned outputs.
architectures.fit: Results can wait and many records need the same operation.
architectures.tradeoff: Efficient bulk processing trades freshness for throughput.
architectures.failure: Partial outputs or stale snapshots: check completeness and publish atomically.
architectures.evaluation: Measure throughput, cost per record, freshness, and failed partitions.
architectures.example: A nightly job refreshes labels across a catalog.

architectures.title: Streaming detection & scoring
architectures.description: Continuously turn events into timely predictions and signals.
architectures.fit: A changing signal needs decisions while still relevant.
architectures.tradeoff: Event ordering and state management complicate operations.
architectures.failure: Late data or feature drift: define event-time windows and monitor distributions.
architectures.evaluation: Measure event-to-decision lag, missed detections, false alarms, and feature freshness.
architectures.example: An equipment monitor flags unusual vibration.

architectures.title: Retrieval & ranking system
architectures.description: Select a useful ordered set of results from a large catalog.
architectures.fit: The product needs ranked recommendations or search results.
architectures.tradeoff: Fast candidate retrieval may eliminate good items before ranking begins.
architectures.failure: Feedback loops or cold starts: evaluate coverage and define exploration policies.
architectures.evaluation: Measure retrieval recall, ranking quality, diversity, and fresh-item coverage.
architectures.example: A reading app orders relevant articles without exposing chat.

architectures.title: Document understanding pipeline
architectures.description: Turn unstructured pages into validated, usable records.
architectures.fit: Information lives in scanned or inconsistently formatted pages.
architectures.tradeoff: Layout variation and ambiguous fields make extraction quality uneven.
architectures.failure: Confidently wrong values: retain page evidence and route uncertain fields to review.
architectures.evaluation: Measure field precision, recall, and correction time across layouts.
architectures.example: A back-office process extracts invoice line items for review.

architectures.title: Router & specialist models
architectures.description: Choose a suitable model or workflow before expensive processing.
architectures.fit: Different task classes benefit from different handling.
architectures.tradeoff: A cheap routing decision can become the main source of downstream mistakes.
architectures.failure: Misrouting or overloaded specialists: test boundary cases and supply a default path.
architectures.evaluation: Measure route confusion, specialist success, latency, and total cost.
architectures.example: A service routes billing and technical questions differently.

architectures.title: Deterministic AI workflow
architectures.description: Use explicit stages and gates around bounded model calls.
architectures.fit: The sequence is known and repeatable.
architectures.tradeoff: Predictable execution adapts poorly to ambiguous requirements.
architectures.failure: Bad intermediate outputs contaminate later steps: validate every stage and stop on failure.
architectures.evaluation: Measure stage pass rates, final success, and rework.
architectures.example: A report workflow extracts evidence, drafts, and checks required sections.

architectures.title: Coordinator & specialist workers
architectures.description: Delegate independent subtasks and reconcile their evidence.
architectures.fit: A problem has separable analysis or research branches.
architectures.tradeoff: Parallelism increases coordination overhead and can duplicate work.
architectures.failure: Conflicting findings or lost provenance: give bounded assignments and merge against original evidence.
architectures.evaluation: Measure coverage, duplication, synthesis quality, and cost against a single-worker baseline.
architectures.example: A research system investigates independent aspects of a topic.

architectures.title: Generate–evaluate–revise
architectures.description: Improve a candidate using explicit criteria and a bounded revision loop.
architectures.fit: Outputs can be assessed against meaningful criteria.
architectures.tradeoff: Extra passes take time and a model evaluator can share the generator’s blind spots.
architectures.failure: Endless revision or superficial improvement: cap iterations and add independent checks.
architectures.evaluation: Measure improvements against held-out judgments, regressions, and iteration count.
architectures.example: A writing workflow checks a draft against an approved outline.

architectures.title: Human approval checkpoint
architectures.description: Separate a proposed decision from permission to execute it.
architectures.fit: Consequential decisions need accountable human judgment.
architectures.tradeoff: Review adds delay and only helps when the evidence is inspectable.
architectures.failure: Rubber-stamping or stale approval: bind approval to the exact action and invalidate changed proposals.
architectures.evaluation: Measure disagreement, corrections, review-queue age, and post-approval changes.
architectures.example: A purchasing assistant prepares an order for a person to approve.
